objective: Review commit b36e708 (ripgrep and fd as user-installed prerequisites) for correctness and regressions.
scope: Worktree /home/user/holyagent-0.3.2-unbundle, branch release/0.3.2/feat/user-installed-search-tools. The change is commit b36e708; review `git diff 3cc15367 b36e708` (source, tests, docs and instruction text without the generated dist: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-holyagent/43946df6-456d-58c6-bea3-7e958fcb9495/scratchpad/unbundle-src.diff; the dist also deletes the vendored binaries and regenerates bundles and agent files). Head 86e6d051 only adds a no-content merge of the integration branch.

Requirement (maintainer, verbatim: "remove the bundling of the executables, list them as dependencies instead", then "I mean dependencies for the users"): HolyAgent stops bundling ripgrep and fd; they become prerequisites the user installs; holyagent rg and holyagent fd run the ones on PATH (fd also as Debian's fdfind); a missing tool fails with install commands per platform; setup and doctor of the Claude plugin and of Pi report them; mise provides them for development and CI; instructions tell agents to fall back to the system search tools when one is missing; docs list them as prerequisites; the updater no longer moves vendored binaries.

Check the CLI wrappers (arguments, stdin, exit codes, Windows .exe lookup through PATHEXT), the doctor/setup reports, the updater after removing the vendored step (mise tools ripgrep and fd moved by it), the mise.toml tool names working on Linux, macOS and Windows CI, and anything still referring to the removed vendor folder.
constraints: Work only inside /home/user/holyagent-0.3.2-unbundle; never check out a branch, commit or make any git write in /home/user/holyagent or any other worktree, and make no edits.
Never start pi or make live Kimi, Codex or OpenAI requests.
Mark each finding blocking or non-blocking, with file:line and a concrete failure scenario. Report in under 450 words.

criteria.text: The change meets the requirement without regressions in the CLI, setup, doctor, build and updater
Tests cover PATH lookup, the fdfind fallback, the missing-tool error and the doctor and setup reports, and would fail without the change

result:
result: b36e708 meets the requirement. I found no blockers. Seven non-blocking findings, listed below.

changed: none (read-only review)

checks:
- `/code-review 3cc15367...b36e708` through the Skill tool -> ran, returned 6 findings, all classed below.
- `bun test` in the worktree -> exit 0, 3443 pass, 1 skip, 0 fail.
- `bun check` -> 0 type errors. `bun lint` -> 0 problems. `bun fmt --no-script --check` -> all 729 files formatted. These ran through the mise tasks.
- Rebuilt both integrations from `git archive HEAD` in the scratchpad and diffed the dist folders against the committed ones -> no differences, so the generated plugin and Pi package are not stale.
- `git ls-remote` confirms tags `15.2.0` (ripgrep) and `v10.5.2` (fd) exist.
- Read but not run:
  - Windows PATHEXT or `.exe` lookup. `findCommand` calls `Bun.which(command, {PATH})`; no test covers Windows, and the fake-script tests are `skipIf(!posix)`.
  - mise installing `ripgrep` and `fd` on the macOS and Windows CI runners.
  - `mise run deps:update` against the network.

findings (all non-blocking):
1. `packages/integrations/claude/tests/plugin.test.ts:792`. The comment "searches with the bundled ripgrep and fd" is stale. Same for `packages/runtime/src/setup/shell.ts:68` ("the way the bundled tools are"). Both come from the code-review run; confirmed.
2. `packages/integrations/claude/src/agents.ts:263-270`. Roles with Bash still get no Grep or Glob. `docs/decisions.md:53` states this on purpose, and the instructions give the fallback to the system `grep` and `find`. On a machine without rg or fd, the first search call fails with exit 4 before the fallback applies. This is a design choice; the root should confirm it. The code-review run reported this as a defect; I rejected it as one.
3. Instruction text fallback wording. The files are the `claude-5.5`, `gpt-6` and `kimi-k3.1` `specialist/working.md`, and the root `search.md` files. They allow `grep` and `find` only after `holyagent rg` or `holyagent fd` fails with ToolMissing. Each session costs one wasted call. This matches the requirement ("fall back when one is missing") and is the minimum the requirement asks for.
4. `packages/runtime/src/setup/search-tools.ts:77-97`. `checkSearchTools` and `reportSearchTools` are near-duplicates that differ only in their line formatters.
5. `packages/runtime/src/cli/tools.ts:32`. `runTool` calls `findCommand` directly, while doctor and setup use `Shell.which`. Both end in `findCommand`, so behavior is identical today. Possible drift only.
6. The Windows lookup is untested. Add a Windows-only test, or run a CI check of `holyagent fd` on the Windows runner.
7. `docs/components.md` and `docs/decisions.md` carry long prose. This is not a defect.

Checked and fine:
- CLI wrappers: arguments pass through unchanged, including `--help`, `-h` and `--`. The program runs in the call's cwd. The exit code and stdio are the program's own. Absent tools exit 4, with an `error:` line that names the program and installs for macOS, Debian/Ubuntu, Fedora, Arch and Windows. `fdfind` is the fallback, and `fd` wins when both exist.
- Doctor and setup:
  - Both report found or missing for rg and fd, in the early-return path too.
  - A missing tool is a `~` warning and never a failure.
  - `--fix` and `--undo` install nothing.
  - Pi and cloud hosts get the same report.
- Updater: the vendor survey, download, checksum and install paths are removed. `MISE_SOURCES` now maps `ripgrep` to BurntSushi/ripgrep and `fd` to sharkdp/fd with prefix `v`, so the existing mise-tools path moves both. Tests cover this at `scripts/update-dependencies.test.ts:160`.
- `mise run vendor` and the `build` dependency on it are removed. No stale `vendor`, `BUNDLED_TOOLS`, `UnsupportedPlatform` or `VENDOR_DIRECTORY` references remain in sources. `docs/` and `AGENTS.md` are updated, and `README.md` lists the prerequisites without breaking its section structure.

evidence:
The change meets the requirement without regressions in the CLI, setup, doctor, build and updater: full `bun test` exit 0 (3443 pass, 0 fail); `bun check`, `bun lint` and `bun fmt --check` clean; dist rebuilt from HEAD with no diff; code read at `packages/runtime/src/cli/tools.ts`, `packages/runtime/src/setup/search-tools.ts`, `packages/runtime/src/setup/doctor.ts`, `packages/runtime/src/setup/steps.ts`, `scripts/update-dependencies.ts` and `mise.toml`. Windows and CI behavior was read, not run.
Tests cover PATH lookup, the fdfind fallback, the missing-tool error and the doctor and setup reports, and would fail without the change: `packages/runtime/tests/tools.test.ts` covers `locateTool` order, the fd-then-fdfind fallback, the ToolMissing exit 4 with all five install commands, argument and exit-code passthrough, and the real rg and fd on PATH. `packages/runtime/tests/setup-search-tools.test.ts` covers the doctor and setup lines for found, missing, fdfind, Pi, cloud and `--fix`/`--undo`. These tests need the new `search-tools.ts` and cannot pass on the base. The Windows `.exe` lookup has no test (finding 6).
